name: Carrion Field

stars.name: Carrion Star
stars.notes: Dim red dwarf casting a perpetual blood-colored light across the system. Low luminosity means the habitable zone—had anything here been habitable—would sit uncomfortably close to the star.

planets.name: Pyre
planets.notes: Tidally locked world with a molten dayside and frozen nightside. The terminator zone shows evidence of weapons scarring—orbital bombardment craters in precise geometric patterns.

planets.name: Charnel
planets.notes: Once a marginally habitable world, now a radiation-soaked ruin. The remains of military installations are visible from orbit—shattered domes, collapsed bunkers, and the fused-glass signatures of nuclear detonations.

planets.name: Cenotaph
planets.notes: Frozen outer world whose ice sheets preserve the wreckage of a fleet action. Hundreds of warship hulls lie entombed in the ice where they crashed during the Battle of Carrion Field.

anomalies.name: The Ghost Broadcast
anomalies.notes: Automated distress signals from destroyed warships continue to transmit on loop decades after the battle. The overlapping transmissions create an eerie cacophony on military frequencies that has never been silenced.

anomalies.name: Radiation Scar
anomalies.notes: Elevated background radiation from extensive nuclear weapons use during the battle. Levels are slowly declining but remain hazardous to prolonged exposure without shielding.

asteroid_belts.name: The Wreck Reef
asteroid_belts.notes: Not a natural formation. This dense field is composed primarily of warship debris, spent munitions, and shattered hull plates from the battle. Salvage teams have cataloged over 900 individual wrecks.

faction_control.notes: Both Terran and Kethrani governments claim the system as a memorial site. Neither maintains a permanent presence. Salvage operations are officially prohibited but occur regularly.

history: Carrion Field was a minor Terran outpost system garrisoned by the 14th Border Regiment until the Kethrani Incursion of 2571 overwhelmed the defenders in a devastating surprise attack that killed all 1.2 million inhabitants of Charnel.

The Terran counterattack, known as the Battle of Carrion Field (2573), was one of the bloodiest engagements in the war. Over 400 warships from both sides were destroyed in a three-day battle that left the system a graveyard. The Terrans reclaimed the system but found nothing left to save.

Since the armistice of 2603, the system has been designated a war memorial by both governments. In practice, neither patrols it effectively, and salvage crews, black-market arms dealers, and war historians all frequent the system for their own purposes.
description: Carrion Field is a tomb. Three worlds orbit a dim red star, but the star's ruddy light illuminates nothing living. Charnel, once home to 1.2 million people, is a radiation-soaked ruin where shattered military installations stand as monuments to the Kethrani surprise attack that killed everyone in a single devastating strike. Cenotaph's ice preserves the hulls of hundreds of warships that crashed during the counterattack. The Wreck Reef between them is a field of debris so dense it registers on navigation charts as a solid obstacle. The automated distress signals still broadcast on loop—an endless, overlapping chorus of dead ships calling for help that will never come.

The Battle of Carrion Field is studied in every military academy in Terran space as an example of both catastrophic intelligence failure and extraordinary tactical valor. The Kethrani struck without warning. The Terran garrison died to the last soldier. The relief fleet arrived two years later and paid for every kilometer of the system in blood, losing 200 ships in three days of fighting before the Kethrani withdrew. The victory, such as it was, left nothing to defend. The system's military value died with its inhabitants, and what remains is significant only as a reminder of what war costs.

Officially, Carrion Field is a protected memorial. In practice, it is a lawless graveyard that attracts salvagers seeking warship-grade materials, historians documenting the battle, and more troubling visitors. Reports persist of ships entering the system and not leaving—whether lost in the dense debris field or taken by unknown parties operating in the Wreck Reef. The Ghost Broadcast, the endless loop of distress signals, has also been noted to occasionally include transmissions that do not match any vessel in the battle registry. Whether these are glitches, hoaxes, or something else remains an open and unsettling question.
